name: media_rss_sweep
what: Live RSS sweep of 8 popular Indian newspapers' section feeds -- Economic Times, Hindu, Hindu Business Line, Times of India, Livemint, Moneycontrol, Business Standard (English) + Amar Ujala (Hindi) -- filtered for investment-intent language (English + Devanagari keywords), matched against real 23-country foreign stock-market rosters (same files layer 42 uses). Full article text pulled only for roster-confirmed hits. Originally a workaround for ET/Hindu/HBL blocking Anthropic's hosted crawler/search infra outright -- runs via subprocess curl from the local machine, which is never blocked (see feedback_economic_times_blocked memory) -- kept as the standard fetch method when extended to more sources for consistency. CAVEAT on the Hindi source: company-name matching only catches names Indian financial press conventionally leaves in Latin script (Apple, Tesla, Toyota); transliterated names (e.g. एप्पल for Apple) are invisible to the shared Latin-script matcher -- partial, not full, non-English coverage. Separate CAVEAT: 'strong' fragment matches on generic industry-descriptive company names (e.g. 'Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp' vs. any article about semiconductor manufacturing in general) still slip through even after the SPAC/share-class filter -- treat every match here as a candidate for human review via its full_text field, not a confirmed lead, same as layer 44's un-reviewed MoU rows.

matches.title: Diversification plan: NMDC scouts for mining assets across four continents
matches.full_text: From South America in the west to Australia in the east, state-owned iron ore giant NMDC is scouting mining assets, including critical minerals, in four continents to meet the future needs of industries such as automotive, renewable energy, electronics, and steel, according to industry sources.NMDC, which caters to India's one-fourth iron ore demand, has set a goal to earn at least 20 per cent of revenues from sale of minerals other than the key steel making raw material.Industry sources stated that the PSU is exploring lithium, copper, cobalt and rare earth blocks in Chile (South America), Australia, Africa, Brazil and parts of Asia.The company is also scouting for limestone mines, dolomite, coking coal and tungsten blocks in the UAE, Oman, Bhutan, and Australia, they said.Acquiring these minerals will allow NMDC to cater to major industries in India on a growth trajectory, such as steel, auto, electronics, renewable energy, aerospace and defence, railway and metros, etc., sources said.When asked for a comment, NMDC said,  Right now, we are a 99.9 per cent iron ore company. We aim to help the growing industries in the country with the maximum of their mineral needs .In an earlier interview with PTI, NMDC Chairman Amitava Mukherjee confirmed the company is working on strategies to diversify into selling other minerals as well. NMDC aims to be India's largest mineral mining company and earn at least 20 per cent of revenue from minerals other than iron ore, he had said.NMDC's expansion aligns directly with government initiatives aimed at securing long-term raw material supplies and reducing import dependency across economic sectors.For the steel sector alone, raw materials account for around 65-70 per cent of steelmaking costs, as per the Ministry of Steel's draft Steel Policy Vision 2047, which aims to reduce import dependence through domestic mining, washery expansion, asset acquisition, long-term supply arrangements, and AI-based optimisation of coal blends.The draft policy said India's objective of increasing the share of manufacturing in the economy, supported by initiatives such as Make in India, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme, semiconductor manufacturing, defence indigenisation and the development of industrial corridors, is expected to significantly expand steel consumption in sectors such as automotive, engineering goods, capital goods, machinery, shipbuilding, renewable energy equipment and defence production.

matches.title: Tata Motors’ €3.91-billion Iveco bid faces make-or-break October 26 test of global ambitions
matches.full_text: From Italy’s industrial heartland to Mumbai’s financial markets, Tata Motors’ €3.91-billion pursuit of truckmaker Iveco faces its make-or-break test today, the scheduled final day for shareholders to tender their shares. Managing Director Girish Wagh is confident of crossing the required 80 per cent acceptance threshold, but activist investor Petrus Advisers is challenging the valuation, Italian Industry Minister Adolfo Urso is demanding industrial safeguards, and Indian brokerages remain divided over financial returns. At stake is whether Tata can overcome these pressures and replicate its landmark Jaguar Land Rover success globally. Only about 35 per cent of Iveco shares had been tendered as of October 22, leaving Tata dependent on a substantial last-minute surge. “As is typically seen in tender offer processes, a significant proportion of shares tend to be tendered towards the very end of the acceptance period, particularly in the final 24 to 48 hours,” Wagh told analysts. “We therefore remain confident of a successful completion of the acquisition.” The combination would create a commercial-vehicle powerhouse spanning India, Europe and the Americas, with approximately €21 billion in annual revenue and sales exceeding 590,000 vehicles. “Tata Motors has demonstrated through Jaguar Land Rover that it can acquire and turn around a global automotive business. Iveco presents a similar opportunity, but weak European demand, acquisition debt and integration costs pose significant risks. The challenge is whether Tata can replicate the JLR success without putting pressure on profitability and its balance sheet,” said Kranti Bathini, Director–Equity Strategy at WealthMills Securities. Urso has pressed Tata to translate its commitments into a concrete industrial revival. Iveco has outlined investments exceeding €76 million across four Italian plants, while unions seek employment safeguards beyond two years and development plans for individual factories. European truckmakers also face sluggish demand, electrification expenditure, emissions-compliance costs and intensifying competition. Davidson Kempner, Syquant Capital, and Petrus Advisers collectively hold about 20.4 per cent of Iveco. If none tender, their combined holdings could prevent Tata from reaching 80 per cent. Petrus argues the offer undervalues Iveco, estimating fair value at approximately €18 per share, around 25% above Tata’s bid. Iveco shareholders approved reducing the acceptance threshold from 95% to 80%. October 26 is the tender deadline, not another vote. Settlement is expected on October 30, subject to conditions, with a possible extension and a scheduled November 2–6 reopening window. Tata secured the regulatory clearances required to launch the offer and increased its bid from €14.10 to €14.40 per share, a 2.1 per cent rise, declaring the price final. matches.title: Cordelia Cruises launches Cordelia Sky, expands fleet to two ships
matches.full_text: Mumbai-headquartered Cordelia Cruises has launched Cordelia Sky, its largest cruise vessel, and commenced commercial sailings on Friday, October 23, 2026. The launch event was attended by representatives from the media and tourism industry. The launch marks the company’s transition from a single-ship operator to a two-ship fleet operator. Its next vessel, Cordelia Sun, is scheduled to be launched in 2027. Addressing the media at the launch, Cordelia Cruises President and CEO Jurgen Bailom said the company had carried more than eight lakh passengers since commencing operations. He said the company was founded with a vision of making cruising a preferred travel option for Indians. “Our goal is, by 2032, to be the top five largest cruise market in the world,” Bailom said. The company, a subsidiary of Waterways Leisure Tourism Ltd, also plans to create 20,000 additional jobs over the next three years. As part of its workforce development initiatives, Cordelia Cruises has started a cadet programme and is moving closer to having its first female captain. Bailom also mentioned about the launch of The Chairman’s Club, a loyalty programme rewarding members. Looking ahead, the company has planned a 34-day cruise from Mumbai to Sydney during the 2028 monsoon season. The itinerary is expected to cover seven countries and 16 ports. Commenting on the impact of geopolitical developments on the cruise business, Bailom highlighted the rising costs of food and fuel. “However, we are still able to manage. But it can’t get worse than it is right now, so we all hope that everything is going to get better soon,” he said. Measuring approximately 260 metres in length (848 feet approximately), Cordelia Sky spans 12 decks and has a gross tonnage of 77,104. The vessel has 1,002 cabins (with double occupancy) across multiple categories, ranging from interior staterooms and ocean-view cabins to balcony mini-suites and suites. The accommodation options include the Chairman’s Suite, described as the largest stateroom onboard. Cordelia Sky offers a range of dining, entertainment and recreational facilities, including a fitness centre, spa and salon, entertainment shows, casinos, a gaming arcade and the 930-seat Marquee Theatre. Casino, poker and more Video arcade, fun gaming for kids and teens The ship houses approximately 10 restaurants, 11 bars and lounges, a pool deck with two swimming pools and five hot tubs, a sports court, meeting rooms and a library. Spaces such as Palace Restaurant, The Crossings and The Great Outdoor Cafe offer complimentary dining. Meanwhile, speciality dining venues include La Cucina, The Great Sushi Bar, The Local Bar & Grill, Topsiders Bar & Grill, Garden Cafe and Spice Route. The Chairman’s Club, Connexions and The Dome lounges. The Sky Bar, Atrium Bar and Just Beans offer additional spaces for relaxation. matches.title: Market recap: Eight of top 10 firms lose Rs 1.55 lakh crore
matches.full_text: NEW DELHI: The combined market valuation of eight of Indiaâs top 10 most valuable companies declined by Rs 1.55 lakh crore last week, with HDFC Bank and Bajaj Finance emerging as the biggest losers. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Larsen & Toubro (L&T) were the only two firms in the top 10 to record gains in their market capitalisation.The decline came as benchmark equity indices registered sharp losses during a holiday-truncated week. The 30-share BSE Sensex fell 1,605.44 points, or 2.15 per cent, while the 50-share NSE Nifty dropped 546.15 points, or 2.36 per cent.Reflecting the weak performance of equities, the total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies declined by Rs 20,78,774.28 crore over four trading sessions to Rs 4,51,83,393.14 crore. The figure stood at Rs 4,72,62,167.42 crore on October 16.Among the eight companies that reported a decline in valuation, HDFC Bank recorded the steepest fall. Its market capitalisation dropped by Rs 55,506.95 crore to Rs 10,67,121.12 crore, while its stock lost 5 per cent over the week.Bajaj Finance followed, with its valuation falling by Rs 34,180.51 crore to Rs 5,77,146.21 crore. Reliance Industries saw its market capitalisation decline by Rs 27,065.08 crore to Rs 16,10,372.11 crore.Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) also registered a substantial fall, with its valuation shrinking by Rs 21,062.24 crore to Rs 4,81,142.58 crore.Bharti Airtel's market capitalisation declined by Rs 9,360.75 crore to Rs 11,79,454.70 crore, while State Bank of India's valuation fell by Rs 4,338.46 crore to Rs 8,83,384.38 crore.Infosys recorded a decline of Rs 2,881.38 crore in its market capitalisation, which stood at Rs 4,68,528.03 crore. ICICI Bank's valuation decreased by Rs 1,276.53 crore to Rs 10,01,594.91 crore.In contrast, TCS and L&T ended the week with gains. TCS added Rs 23,517.56 crore to its market capitalisation, taking it to Rs 9,14,652.52 crore. L&T's valuation rose by Rs 1,788.66 crore to Rs 5,01,513.72 crore.Despite the weekly decline, Reliance Industries remained India's most valuable company, followed by Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank. matches.title: L'Oreal sees India biz gaining momentum; expands skincare, online presence
matches.full_text: French cosmetics major L'Oreal sees its India business "doing a great turnaround", driven by improving team capabilities, increasing localisation, accelerating online commerce and rising demand for haircare and skincare products, said its global Chief Executive Officer Nicolas Hieronimus.India recorded a "double-digit growth" in the group's consumer products division business in the September quarter. Besides, its "emerging markets delivered spectacular growth, particularly in Brazil and India" in the professional products, according to the company's latest earnings update.L'Oreal's SAPMENA-SSA region posted adjusted like-for-like growth of 19.2 per cent in the third quarter of 2026, with India and Indonesia "further accelerated", driven by haircare and skincare, the cosmetics major said.The region comprises South Asia Pacific, the Middle East, North Africa and Sub-Saharan Africa, and is one of L'Oreal's key operational and financial reporting regions.In the earnings call, Hieronimus, who visited India a few weeks ago, said the country was witnessing a strong turnaround, supported by improvements in team capabilities and a greater focus on developing products tailored to local consumers."India, where I was just a couple of weeks ago, is doing a great turnaround there, both in terms of teams' quality. We create for India much more than we did before," said Hieronimus.The company is also accelerating its online commerce strategy, particularly quick commerce, while expanding its skincare brands CeraVe and La Roche-Posay into new cities to tap the growing demand for specialised skincare products."We are accelerating in commerce, with a focus on quick commerce, which is an important part of the e-commerce market there," he said.L'Oreal is also expanding its presence in the dermatological beauty segment, with its skincare brand CeraVe gaining traction and entering new cities in India."India is one of the countries where CeraVe is still a baby brand, but growing fast and expanding to new cities," Hieronimus said.The company has also launched La Roche-Posay, another brand in its dermatological beauty portfolio, in India.
